title: CHAPTER 13: QUICK REFERENCE — ADDITIONAL IMPORTANT FACTS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Somnath Temple stands as the first among the twelve holy Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva.
Sabarmati Ashram served as one of the main residences of Mahatma Gandhi and the starting node of the 1930 Dandi March.
GPSC is the constitutional body responsible for recruiting officers for civil services in Gujarat under Articles 315–323.
Gujarat's river system is primarily divided into major west-flowing rivers like Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, and Sabarmati.
Various statutory commissions and state committees shape the administrative and policy framework of Gujarat.
Somnath is the first and most sacred of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva.
Located at Prabhas Patan in Veraval, Gir Somnath district.
Destroyed and rebuilt 17 times according to tradition.
Mahmud of Ghazni plundered it in 1025 CE.
The current temple was built under the initiative of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel after independence; inaugurated on December 11, 1995 by President Shankar Dayal Sharma.
K.M. Munshi played a major role in the temple's reconstruction; he wrote the book 'Jaya Somnath' based on its history.
Founded by Gandhi in 1917 on the banks of Sabarmati River, Ahmedabad.
The Dandi March started from here on March 12, 1930.
Gandhi lived here from 1917 to 1930.
Also known as Satyagraha Ashram and later Harijan Ashram.
Now a national monument and museum.

items: Established under Article 315 of the Constitution of India.
Conducts recruitment for Group 1 and Group 2 (Class I and Class II) state government services.
Conducts Gujarat Administrative Service (GAS), Gujarat Police Service (GPS), and other exams.
Headquartered in Ahmedabad.
Gujarat Police is headed by the Director General of Police (DGP).
Gujarat has multiple police ranges divided into zones.
Sub-Inspector (SI) recruitment is conducted through GPSC/Lok Rakshak Dal Board.
Police training: Karai Police Training Centre, Gandhinagar; Junagadh Police Training College.
Gujarat Forensic Sciences University (GFSU): World's first forensic sciences university; Gandhinagar.

blocks.content: 13.6 Important Committees and Commissions Related to Gujarat

items: Questions on Sabarmati Ashram frequently target its establishment year (1917) and its role in the Dandi March.
Constitutional provisions (Articles 315 to 323) regarding the State Public Service Commission (GPSC) are high-yield exam topics.
Origin points and gulfs where major rivers like Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, and Sabarmati drain are repeatedly tested in GPSC prelims.
Justice V.S. Dave Commission: Investigated the 2002 Gujarat riots.
Nanavati-Shah Commission: Another commission examining the 2002 communal riots.
State Finance Commission: Set up every 5 years for devolution of funds to local bodies.

blocks.content: 13.7 Notable Inventions / Contributions from Gujarat to India

items: White Revolution / Operation Flood: Dr. Verghese Kurien from Anand, Gujarat transformed India into the world's largest milk producer.
Space Program: Vikram Sarabhai (Ahmedabad) is the father of India's space program.
Non-violence philosophy: Mahatma Gandhi's Ahimsa and Satyagraha changed the world.
Diamond polishing industry: Surat's craftsmen made India a global diamond hub.
Cooperative movement: Gujarat's cooperative model (AMUL) inspired cooperatives across India.
